Welcome to my blog

I have been building websites and small products for a few years now, and for most of that time the lessons stayed in my head or in scattered notes. This blog is where I plan to put them in order.

Expect short, practical posts: how I build things, what went wrong along the way, and the small habits that made the work easier. I will write about web development, design details, and the process of turning an idea into something people can actually use.

Oct 10, 20264 min read

Building a portfolio with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript

When I started planning this site, the easy option was to reach for a framework. I chose plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript instead, for one reason: I wanted a site I could open, read and change without a build step.

What stayed simple

A single file loads fast, works offline once opened, and is easy to host anywhere. Theme switching, project filtering and scroll animations all turned out to need only a few dozen lines each.

What took real effort

  • Keeping spacing and typography consistent across every section
  • Making each section work properly on small phones
  • Keeping animations subtle enough that they never get in the way

The lesson was that the fundamentals go a long way. A careful layout and honest, readable content matter more than any library.

Sep 28, 20265 min read

Five habits that made learning web development faster

There is no shortcut to getting good at building for the web, but some routines make the same hours count for more. These are the five that worked for me.

  • Build something small every week, even if nobody will see it
  • Read other people's code and ask why it was written that way
  • Break things on purpose to learn how they fail
  • Write down what you learn in your own words
  • Share work before it feels ready

None of this is complicated. The hard part is repeating it long enough for the progress to show.

Sep 15, 20264 min read

Small UI details that make a site feel premium

Most sites that feel polished are not doing anything exotic. They are getting a handful of small things right, consistently.

Spacing first

Generous, even spacing does more for a layout than any decoration. When in doubt, add more room around content, not more elements.

Motion with restraint

Animation should guide attention, not demand it. Short fades and gentle movement on scroll feel smooth; anything longer starts to feel slow.

Typography

Pick two typefaces at most, keep line lengths comfortable, and let size and weight create the hierarchy.
